<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אייר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918633_theRebbe_459" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_99_D7_99_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918633_theRebbe_459__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the Sages' statement about the crowns tied to Israel for saying "we will do" before "we will hear," interpreting "naaseh" as acceptance of the yoke of Heaven and "nishma" as acceptance of the yoke of commandments, analogous to ratzo and shov.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood based on what our Sages, of blessed memory, said:</t>
    <t s="2">"At the time that Israel preceded 'we will do' to 'we will hear,' the ministering angels came and tied two crowns to each and every Jew, one corresponding to 'we will do' and one corresponding to 'we will hear.'"</t>
    <t s="3">And the precise point in this is known,</t>
    <t s="4">that at the beginning of the statement, "at the time that they preceded etc.," it implies that this tying of two crowns to them was because they preceded "we will do" to "we will hear,"</t>
    <t s="5">while at the conclusion of the statement it says, "one corresponding to 'we will do' and one corresponding to 'we will hear,'"</t>
    <t s="6">meaning that the two crowns are for "we will do" and "we will hear" themselves.</t>
    <t s="7">And the Rebbe Maharash explains in his maamar beginning "B'sha'ah shehikdimu" said in Parshas Bamidbar one hundred years ago,</t>
    <t s="8">that "naaseh" is the acceptance of the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven, and "nishma" is the acceptance of the yoke of the commandments.</t>
    <t s="9">And the matter of the precedence of "naaseh" to "nishma" is as the statement of our Sages, of blessed memory:</t>
    <t s="10">"Why did the portion of 'Shema' precede 'V'hayah im shamoa'? So that one should first accept upon himself the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven, and afterwards accept upon himself the yoke of the commandments."</t>
    <t s="11">And he explains there,</t>
    <t s="12">that the first portion is ratzo (running/ecstasy) and self-sacrifice, and the second portion is shov (return).</t>
    <t s="13">And just as in ratzo and shov,</t>
    <t s="14">first there must be ratzo and then shov,</t>
    <t s="15">similarly it is regarding acceptance of the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven and acceptance of the yoke of the commandments,</t>
    <t s="16">that before the acceptance of the yoke of the commandments there must be the acceptance of the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="17">And based on this, he explains there</t>
    <t s="18">what our Sages said, "at the time that they preceded etc.,"</t>
    <t s="19">that even though the two crowns are corresponding to "naaseh" and "nishma" themselves</t>
    <t s="20">[one corresponding to "naaseh" and one corresponding to "nishma"],</t>
    <t s="21">because in order for there to be the shov</t>
    <t s="22">(nishma),</t>
    <t s="23">there must be the precedence of ratzo</t>
    <t s="24">(naaseh).</t>
    <t s="25">And he continues in the maamar there,</t>
    <t s="26">that this tying of two crowns to them</t>
    <t s="27">(specifically crowns),</t>
    <t s="28">is,</t>
    <t s="29">because a crown is a makif (encompassing light),</t>
    <t s="30">sovev (surrounding),</t>
    <t s="31">and there are two matters in this,</t>
    <t s="32">the ascent of the memaleh (pervading light) into the sovev, and the drawing down of the sovev into the memaleh.</t>
    <t s="33">And seemingly the intention is,</t>
    <t s="34">that the crown corresponding to "naaseh"</t>
    <t s="35">(ratzo)</t>
    <t s="36">is the ascent of the memaleh into the sovev, and the crown corresponding to "nishma"</t>
    <t s="37">(shov)</t>
    <t s="38">is the drawing down of the sovev into the memaleh.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section clarifies that the two crowns are specifically tied due to the precedence of "naaseh" to "nishma," because the crown for "nishma" (shov) is only possible when preceded by "naaseh" (ratzo), as the encompassing light of the crown is above connection to worlds.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that this which the maamar adds, that this tying of two crowns to them is because a crown is a makif,</t>
    <t s="2">is,</t>
    <t s="3">because from the language of our Sages, "at the time that they preceded etc., they tied two crowns to them," it implies that the precise point of the precedence of "naaseh" to "nishma" is related to the two crowns that are corresponding to "naaseh" and "nishma"</t>
    <t s="4">(and not to "naaseh" and "nishma" themselves),</t>
    <t s="5">therefore he explains that a crown is a makif and sovev, and the two crowns are two matters in the sovev,</t>
    <t s="6">because this is an explanation of the fact that the tying of the two crowns was specifically through their having preceded "naaseh" to "nishma"</t>
    <t s="7">(as will be explained below).</t>
    <t s="8">And this which he explains beforehand, that the need to precede "naaseh" to "nishma" is because "naaseh" and "nishma" are like ratzo and shov,</t>
    <t s="9">is an explanation of the fact that the crown corresponding to "nishma"</t>
    <t s="10">(makif and sovev)</t>
    <t s="11">is specifically when the "nishma" is after the precedence of "naaseh."</t>
    <t s="12">Because makif and sovev is above any connection to worlds,</t>
    <t s="13">and since "nishma" is shov and a drawing down below,</t>
    <t s="14">therefore,</t>
    <t s="15">this tying of a crown</t>
    <t s="16">(makif and sovev which is above the world)</t>
    <t s="17">corresponding to "nishma"</t>
    <t s="18">(a drawing down below)</t>
    <t s="19">is specifically because the "nishma" was after the precedence of "naaseh,"</t>
    <t s="20">ratzo and ascent above.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section distinguishes between two levels of encompassing light: the makif of keter, which is truly above connection to the internal, unlike the makif of gulgalta which is related to it, analogous to the two levels of will in a person.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And explanation is needed,</t>
    <t s="2">after all, the entire matter of acceptance of a yoke,</t>
    <t s="3">even the acceptance of the yoke of the commandments</t>
    <t s="4">(nishma),</t>
    <t s="5">is bittul (self-nullification),</t>
    <t s="6">for the matter of bittul is that a person goes out of his own existence,</t>
    <t s="7">and the tying of the crown corresponding to "nishma" is specifically when the "nishma" is after the precedence of "naaseh."</t>
    <t s="8">And the explanation of this can be said based on what is known,</t>
    <t s="9">that the makif of keter is the true makif that is above the makif that is related to the internal.</t>
    <t s="10">For this is the difference between keter and gulgalta,</t>
    <t s="11">that gulgalta is a makif that is related to the internal,</t>
    <t s="12">analogous to the skull in a person which encompasses the brain but is related to it,</t>
    <t s="13">for the skull is from his body like the brain.</t>
    <t s="14">And the makif of keter is a makif that is above any connection to the internal,</t>
    <t s="15">analogous to a crown in its simple sense, which is a circlet upon the brain and skull and has no connection to them</t>
    <t s="16">(for the crown is made of precious stones and not from the person's body).</t>
    <t s="17">And although gulgalta is also called by the name "keter,"</t>
    <t s="18">this is in a general sense,</t>
    <t s="19">but the essence of the crown is the makif that is not related to the internal</t>
    <t s="20">(which is above the makif of gulgalta).</t>
    <t s="21">And this is analogous to the will in a person,</t>
    <t s="22">for will is a makif upon all the faculties and limbs,</t>
    <t s="23">and it has two levels.</t>
    <t s="24">The will to do some thing through one's faculties,</t>
    <t s="25">for this will, although it rules over all the faculties because it encompasses them,</t>
    <t s="26">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="27">this very fact that it desires the action of the faculties,</t>
    <t s="28">is proof that it has a connection to them — this is the makif of gulgalta.</t>
    <t s="29">And it is a descent relative to the will itself as it is above the will to do — this is the makif of keter.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
